as_written_in_papers.quote: A homozygous mutation in the LCAT gene (c.355G>C, p.Gly119Arg) was identified.

cases.statement: Three carriers in one Chinese family with parental consanguinity: the affected homozygous proband and his two heterozygous, asymptomatic parents.

people.label: patient (proband)
people.key_phenotypes: corneal opacity since childhood; nephrotic syndrome; markedly reduced HDL-C; glomerular lipid deposition on renal biopsy; anemia (attributed by the authors mainly to co-inherited alpha0-thalassemia trait)

quotes.quote: The patient is a 50-year-old Chinese male who was admitted with progressive edema in both lower limbs for the past 2 months.
He had a history of bilateral corneal opacity since childhood and long-standing mild anemia-related symptoms, although no systematic diagnostic work-up or regular follow-up had been done.

Laboratory investigations revealed features characteristic of nephrotic syndrome: serum albumin was 26.2 g/L, 24-h urinary protein excretion was 11.82 g/d, and the urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio was 5949.18 μg/mg.
The blood lipid profile was abnormal: triglycerides 1.73 mmol/L, total cholesterol 3.85 mmol/L, HDL-C 0.43 mmol/L, and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol 1.69 mmol/L.
Histopathological examination revealed glomerular lipid deposition, confirming the diagnosis of LCAT deficiency-related renal damage (Figures 3–5).

phenotype_specificity.statement: Corneal opacity, very low HDL-C, nephrotic syndrome and characteristic glomerular lipid deposition on biopsy; autoantibodies and anti-PLA2R were normal. A hereditary kidney disease gene panel was used (results for other genes not stated). The microcytic anemia was attributed to a second genetic finding, alpha0-thalassemia trait (HBA: --SEA/αα).

quotes.quote: Autoantibodies (including antinuclear antibodies, anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies), immunoglobulins, light chains, and anti-phospholipase A2 receptor antibodies were all normal.
Based on the pathological findings, targeted next-generation sequencing of hereditary kidney disease genes was performed using a custom panel.

Combined with the typical clinical manifestations (corneal opacity, significant decrease of HDL-C, nephrotic syndrome) and pathological features of renal tissue, the patient was finally diagnosed as familial LCAT deficiency.

segregation.statement: Both parents are heterozygous and asymptomatic. The only sibling, a reportedly healthy sister, declined genetic testing. No other affected relatives.

quotes.quote: Sanger sequencing validated this variant in the proband and both parents, confirming heterozygous carrier status in the parents and autosomal recessive inheritance (Figure 6).
He has one sister who is reportedly healthy with no history of anemia, renal disease, or visual disturbances; however, she declined genetic testing.

in_trans.statement: Homozygous; both parents tested by Sanger sequencing and found heterozygous, consistent with true homozygosity. Parents are consanguineous.

quotes.quote: Sanger sequencing validated this variant in the proband and both parents, confirming heterozygous carrier status in the parents and autosomal recessive inheritance (Figure 6).
His family history indicated consanguinity between his parents.

functional.statement: No functional assay; the authors state LCAT enzyme activity could not be measured.

quotes.quote: The follow-up period is short, and LCAT enzyme activity could not be measured because the test is unavailable in our region.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Missense (c.355G>C, p.(Gly119Arg)). The paper describes the disease as due to dysfunction of the LCAT enzyme.

quotes.quote: LCAT deficiency is a rare autosomal recessive disorder caused by the dysfunction of the LCAT enzyme, leading to impaired cholesterol esterification and subsequent lipoprotein metabolism abnormalities (Strazzella et al., 2021).

computational_predictions.statement: PolyPhen-2 0.998 (probably damaging), SIFT 0.00 (deleterious), CADD Phred 28.5, as reported by the authors.

quotes.quote: PolyPhen-2 scored 0.998 (probably damaging), SIFT scored 0.00 (deleterious), and CADD Phred score was 28.5 (clinically significant, >20) (Table 1).
| CADD | https://cadd.gs.washington.edu/ | 28.5 | >20 = clinically significant | Clinically significant |

population_data_in_papers.statement: No frequency is given for this variant; the methods only name the population databases consulted. The authors call the variant novel.

quotes.quote: Population frequencies were obtained from public databases (1000 Genomes, gnomAD, ExAC), and variants were interpreted according to ACMG guidelines.

authors_classification.statement: No ACMG class is given; the authors say the in-silico predictions support pathogenicity.

quotes.quote: These computational predictions consistently support the pathogenic nature of the c.355G>C (p.Gly119Arg) variant.

concerns: Second genetic diagnosis in the same person: alpha0-thalassemia trait (HBA: --SEA/αα), which the authors use to explain the microcytic anemia.
LCAT enzyme activity was not measured.
No transcript is stated; reads were aligned to GRCh37/hg19.
Parents are consanguineous, so homozygosity for a rare variant is expected under shared ancestry; results for other genes on the kidney panel are not stated.
The two parent rows (LCAT-ID0169, LCAT-ID0170) are the father and mother, but the paper does not say which row is which.
notes_for_panel: Homozygous missense in a consanguineous family with biopsy-proven LCAT-type glomerular lipid deposition, corneal opacity and very low HDL-C; both parents heterozygous and asymptomatic. In-silico scores reported; no functional or enzyme-activity data.
